clue.text: Do they indicate that crime does pay?

definitions.text: Do they indicate that crime does pay?

parts.words: Do they indicate that crime does pay?
parts.note: the biblical phrase about the earnings of wrongdoing is read literally, as if sinners drew a salary

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether lawbreaking is profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says these earnings are death; the clue takes the word for pay at face value, as if crime were a salaried job.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical idiom literally names payment received for wrongdoing, which is what the clue's question describes.

clue.text: Reserves we held in capital

indicators.note: read as re-serves, the words are served up again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recalls holding back reserve funds in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserves' looks like a noun for stored funds or substitutes, but split as re-serves it signals rearranging WE HELD IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city is the seat of national government, so it is a capital.

clue.text: Letter from abroad bound to have shown sympathy

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, foreign to English
bound means tied up

explanation.surface: A foreign letter obliged someone to show compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel and display compassion for someone is a synonym of having felt pity for them.

clue.text: Report a fringe fashion

definitions.meaning: a report is a loud noise such as a gunshot
in American usage a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead

explanation.surface: A news item about an unusual hairstyle trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringe' suggests something marginal, but it is the hair over the forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a sharp explosive noise and a hairstyle of straight-cut fringe share the one short word.

clue.text: One can set out on donkey seeking help

indicators.note: in a down clue the donkey comes on top, so it is written first

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone climbs on a donkey to go and look for aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I (One) with CAN SET to make ISTANCE, which follows ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Help and aid given to someone is a direct synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Cries from clumsy seamen on prow of boat

indicators.note: in a down clue the B is placed on top of the seamen
the prow is the front of a boat, so its first letter is taken

parts.note: a lubber is a clumsy, inexperienced sailor, as in landlubber

explanation.surface: Awkward sailors standing at the front of a vessel shout out.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to weep noisily, so the verb form means cries.

clue.text: Sailor, doubly evil

parts.note: evil as a noun gives sin
evil as an adjective gives bad, the second of the two

explanation.surface: A seaman described as wicked twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' asks for two words meaning evil, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary seafarer of the Arabian Nights tales is a famous sailor.

clue.text: Old notes used after silver

indicators.note: the notes are placed after the silver

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
E and D are musical notes

explanation.surface: Antique banknotes spent following a silver payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone advanced in years is described as elderly, a synonym of old.

clue.text: They're a blend of the main races

indicators.note: blending mixes the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that a nation is a mix of the principal ethnic groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blend of' rearranges MAIN RACES; the definition is just 'They're', the people the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paints the US population as a melting pot, so 'they' are its people.

clue.text: Prone to mendacity

definitions.meaning: prone means stretched out flat, face down
mendacity is the habit of telling untruths

explanation.surface: A person inclined to tell falsehoods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone to' reads as 'inclined to', but 'Prone' is a definition on its own and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stretched out flat and telling falsehoods, matching each definition.

clue.text: Going round, showing opposition to the current trend

definitions.meaning: swirling in a circle, as water does

definitions.text: showing opposition to the current trend
definitions.meaning: a swirl of water runs against the main flow of a stream

explanation.surface: A contrarian who circulates while resisting fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current trend' reads as fashion, but the current is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool swirls round and runs counter to the main stream's flow, fitting both senses.

clue.text: One doctor needs one bed — drunk!

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
again I for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital with one doctor needing a single bed for a drunk patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, so the past participle means drunk, as in consumed.

clue.text: Bribed not to squeal?

definitions.meaning: oiling someone's palm means paying them off
lubricated machinery stops squeaking, with a nod to an informer kept quiet

explanation.surface: Someone was paid off so they would not inform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeal' looks like informing, but it is also the noise an unlubricated hinge makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A greased palm is a bribe, and greased hinges stop squealing, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Having a symptom of fever — rash?

definitions.meaning: feverish people have a burning forehead
rash means impetuous, acting without thought

explanation.surface: A patient with a temperature who has also broken out in spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin symptom alongside fever, but it means reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a burning head, and idiomatically impetuous or reckless, fitting both halves.

clue.text: Their union offers security

parts.note: describes a two-part dress fastener whose parts link to hold clothing closed, read like a couple or a trade union

explanation.surface: A trade union or marriage providing protection.
explanation.definitionFit: The two pieces of this fastener join together to secure a garment.

clue.text: Seagoing vandals

parts.note: wreckers at sea, describing a class of fast naval warship

explanation.surface: Pirates or hooligans on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The warship's name literally means wreckers, so they are vandals that go to sea.

clue.text: Show resolution and reject pleas for disarmament

definitions.meaning: to hold firm to one's position
taken literally, to keep hold of one's weapons

explanation.surface: A nation stands firm and refuses calls to give up arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means holding firm under pressure, and literally means keeping one's weapons.

clue.text: Put tar underneath vessel

parts.note: tar is a sailor, dragged under a ship's hull as an old naval punishment

explanation.surface: Instructions to apply pitch to the bottom of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tar' looks like the black waterproofing, but it is a crossword word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical naval punishment dragged an offending seaman beneath the ship's hull.

clue.text: Pat, due to makeover, becomes trendy

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, here the letters

explanation.surface: Pat gets a fashionable new look thanks to a style makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: Being current and modern is a synonym for being fashionable or trendy.

clue.text: End a Metro trip to see it?

definitions.text: End a Metro trip to see it?

indicators.note: a trip suggests the letters stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Get off the Paris underground to go and see a landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges END A METRO; the whole clue describes ending a Paris Metro ride to visit the cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The great Gothic cathedral in Paris is a sight one rides the Metro to visit.

clue.text: Unfortunate soldier trapped in overturned vehicle

indicators.note: the soldier is enclosed inside the vehicle
in a down clue an overturned word is read upwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier caught in a vehicle that has rolled over suffers a sad fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns CART to TRAC, and GI goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calamitous or regrettable is tragic, a synonym of unfortunate.

clue.text: Supply a trace out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Provide a trace that has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide food or what is needed is to cater, a synonym of supply.

clue.text: A minor tax

definitions.meaning: a child placed in someone's care is their ward

explanation.surface: A small levy, or a tax on young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A minor' looks like a small adjective, but it means a child in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a child in one's care and a fee or levy demanded.

clue.text: Washed up when every one was in bed

indicators.note: every one is placed inside the bed

parts.note: taken as written
each means every one

explanation.surface: Everyone was tucked up when something came ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat or whale stranded on shore has been beached, synonymous with washed up.

clue.text: Wooden support for the shaft

definitions.meaning: a timber joist across a building
a shaft of light, a ray

explanation.surface: A timber prop for the mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaft' looks like a mine or lift shaft, but it is a ray of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a horizontal timber and a ray of light.

clue.text: When people may collect in the streets

definitions.text: When people may collect in the streets

parts.words: When people may collect in the streets
parts.note: suggests crowds gathering, but means charity collectors with tins giving out little stickers

explanation.surface: A time when crowds gather outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: A British charity fundraising day when collectors in the street hand donors small paper stickers.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity fundraising day is when volunteers collect money from passers-by.

clue.text: A pair of braces

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds, so two of them makes a number

explanation.surface: Trouser suspenders.
explanation.walkthrough: Braces are British for trouser suspenders, but a brace is also two of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Two braces of two each makes this number.

clue.text: Something cast in gold — the last word in France

indicators.note: the cast object goes inside the gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is cast, as in dice or 'the die is cast'

explanation.surface: A gold-cast item described as the ultimate in French style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last word' suggests the height of fashion, but it is the farewell said in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell is literally the final thing said on parting.

clue.text: A shaver of today — or tomorrow?

definitions.text: A shaver of today — or tomorrow?

parts.words: A shaver of today — or tomorrow?
parts.note: a young shaver is a lad who will only start shaving in the future

explanation.surface: A razor of the present or the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaver' looks like a razor, but 'young shaver' is an old phrase for a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A young shaver is a boy, who will be shaving tomorrow.
